records.title: Society and the Oceans
records.header: SMEA 103 Society and the Oceans (5) NSc/SSc, DIV
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 103 Society and the Oceans (5) NSc/SSc, DIV Explores the social, justice, and policy dimensions of the ocean environment and ocean management policy. Pays attention to how human values, institutions, culture, and history shape environmental issues and policy responses. Examines case studies and influential frameworks, such as the ocean as "tragedy of the commons." Offered: jointly with ENVIR 103/JSIS B 103; Sp.

records.title: Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis
records.header: SMEA 201 Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis (5) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 201 Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis (5) SSc/NSc, DIV Examines climate change, its causes and impacts (on ecosystems, water availability, extreme weather, communities, health, and food) globally, nationally, and locally. Surveys its solutions (mitigation, adaptation, migration, and just transition), actors that implement them (governments, firms, NGOs, activists, communities, individuals) and approaches they use (regulation, markets, planning, innovation, social movements, behavioral change). Offered: jointly with ENVIR 201; Sp.

records.title: International Organizations and Ocean Management
records.header: SMEA 407 International Organizations and Ocean Management (3) SSc
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 407 International Organizations and Ocean Management (3) SSc Surveys the manner in which international regimes and organizations govern and manage ocean use. Primary emphasis is on the analysis of the effectiveness of regimes and of processes that support or constrain organizations in different issues or regions, such as climate change or the Arctic.

records.title: Environmental Degradation in the Tropics
records.header: SMEA 433 Environmental Degradation in the Tropics (5) SSc/NSc
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 433 Environmental Degradation in the Tropics (5) SSc/NSc Considers theories and controversies of environmental degradation in the tropics, ecological and social case studies of Central American rain forests and Southeast Asian coral reefs, and implications of environmental management techniques. Offered: jointly with ENVIR 433/JSIS B 433.

records.title: Practicum in Community-Engaged Ecocultural Research
records.header: SMEA 473 Practicum in Community-Engaged Ecocultural Research (3) SSc, DIV
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 473 Practicum in Community-Engaged Ecocultural Research (3) SSc, DIV Theory and methods for developing community partnerships for environmental research. Readings in feminist science and technology studies, Indigenous studies, political ecology and reflexive writing support development of a community engagement protocol on a topic of interest. Basic legal research, reading, and briefing selected judicial opinions. Participatory case study component. Designed for non-law graduate and advanced undergraduate students. records.title: Pacific Recreation and Tourism Issues
records.header: SMEA 485 Pacific Recreation and Tourism Issues (3) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.departmentName: School of Marine and Environmental Affairs (SMEA)
records.text: SMEA 485 Pacific Recreation and Tourism Issues (3) SSc/NSc, DIV Examines how marine tourism links people to one another and to the environment. Utilizes concepts from cultural anthropology, sociology, political science, geography, ecology, conservation biology, and planning. Topics include: ecotourism, ethnic tourism, marine parks and protected area, fisheries, sustainable development, tourism ethics, and marine environmental education.
